verdict.rationale: three.js is very widely adopted, with about 12.2M weekly npm downloads. That means abundant public code and examples, backed by an official examples gallery, a manual and source-repo starter code. It also ships LLM-targeted docs: a root llms.txt, a docs llms.txt with an explicit 'Instructions for Large Language Models' section, and a 363 KB llms-full.txt. The 'stable' part is weaker. The package is still at 0.x (0.186.0) with per-release migration guides, and llms.txt has to steer models away from outdated CDN patterns toward import maps and from GLSL hacks toward TSL. That suggests models trained on older code can emit stale patterns. Missing for 10: evidence of API stability across versions (frequent breaking migrations are implied), and independent hands-on evidence that LLM-generated three.js code works on the first try.
